newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to deal appropriately with forex moves--MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan to deal appropriately with forex moves--MOF.

text.p: Japan will deal appropriately with movements in the foreign exchange market while keeping careful watch over daily movements, Vice Finance Minister Tadashi Ogawa told a news conference on Thursday.
"We will keep sufficient watch over daily market movements and will deal appropriately when the time is right, in line with our basic thinking," he said.

Ogawa declined to comment on specific currency levels when he was asked whether the current dollar/yen rate would eventually lead to trade imbalances, which the Group of Seven (G7) nations had agreed to avoid.
Ogawa said, however, that the G7 monetary authorities are united in their thinking and in how they will deal with movements in the currency markets.
He said it was "extremely important" that the G7 nations had been able to share a common understanding to avoid currency rates that would lead to trade imbalances.
He also stressed the importance of the G7 understanding that it was undesirable for currency rates to deviate from fundamentals.
The same understanding was also shared between Japan and the United States, in that they would continue their close cooperation with regard to the currency markets.
Ogawa said that Japan's economic condition after the sales tax increase on April 1 was as expected.
He added that he did not think upcoming economic data would show that Japan's economic recovery was faltering.
